input.question: Why do we urinate even when we are dehydrated/thirsty?
input.ground_truth: Let's start by differentiating between thirsty and dehydration. Thirst is wanting water, dehydration is running out of water. At later stage dehydration your renal system shuts down and waste backs up. You eventually die. You pee because you're using water to get rid of bad stuff in your system, not because you have too much water.

Question: Why do we urinate even when we are dehydrated/thirsty?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a little house, and inside your house, there are tiny pipes that help get rid of things your body doesn’t need anymore. One of those things is pee (urine).

Even if you don’t have a lot of water in your body (because you’re thirsty), your body still makes a little bit of pee. That’s because your body is always working to clean out tiny bits of stuff that are left over from the food you eat and the things your body makes.

So, even when you’re thirsty and don’t have much water, your body still needs to get rid of those little bits, so you pee a little bit. But when you drink water, your body makes more pee!

So, you pee even when you’re thirsty, because your body is always trying to stay clean inside. 💧🚽
